tasks.title: Fix phase-read contract and explicit multi-active task starts
tasks.description:
Repair two cross-harness regressions observed while operating the planner in heca. First, `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` registers `planner-phase-show` (around lines 630–644) and calls `text(..., { linkedRequirements })`: Claude Code renders this sparse structured payload and hides the otherwise correct text content containing the phase title and long description. Define a complete structured phase read model (identity/ref, title, summary, description when `full=true`, derived status, task count, and `linkedRequirements`) and validate it through the real MCP harness as Claude Code consumes it. Second, `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` task-start logic (around lines 1019–1084) and the matching `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts` logic (around lines 3924–3980) treat `recommendNextTask()` as a hard authorization gate. When multiple tasks are already `in-progress`, its intentionally advisory `conflict` result prevents an explicitly requested task (such as T416) from starting. Preserve automatic-selection safety and conflict warnings, but allow an explicit task-start request for a valid ready task without requiring unrelated active tasks to be falsely completed/blocked. Confirm behavior is consistent in MCP and Pi, preserve dependency and terminal-state protection, and add regression tests using the real MCP server and Pi host fixture.

---
**Completion summary:**
Fixed the cross-harness regressions locally (not committed). `planner-phase-show` in `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` now returns a complete structured `phase` model (human ref, title, summary, derived status, task count, and description on `full=true`) alongside linked requirements, so Claude Code no longer hides the phase description by rendering only `{linkedRequirements}`. Added a real MCP regression test that reads the structured response as a Claude-style client.

Added the harness-agnostic `checkExplicitTaskStart` in `packages/plan-core/src/task-selection.ts`. MCP and Pi task-start handlers now use it to enforce real availability/dependency rules while treating priority, a single active task, and multiple active tasks as advisories rather than hard denials for an explicit task reference. Responses distinguish priority, active-task, and active-work-conflict advisories. This allows an explicitly chosen task such as T416 to start without falsely closing unrelated tasks. Also fixed approved deviation activation so it remains reliable even when recommendation output points at already active work; preserved the existing approved waiting-task exception.

Added unit + real MCP/Pi adapter regression coverage. Validation passed: targeted suite 59/59, `pnpm check`, and `pnpm test` 359/359 (baseline coverage line 82.92%, branch 73.4%, functions 78.7%). Modified files remain uncommitted on `next`: core selector/tests, MCP handler/tests, Pi handler/tests.
tasks.notes: While executing the cross-harness regression suite, an existing deviation test exposed a coupled third defect: `recommendNextTask()` returns the current active task before inspecting an approved deviation, so starting the deviation’s temporary task after another explicit start does not transition the deviation to `active`. The task-start fix will activate an approved matching deviation directly from persisted `workDeviations`, rather than relying on advisory recommendation output. This preserves the deviation/resume lifecycle under explicit multi-active starts.
